questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To get a deeper understandig of the spanish culture and learning the language fluently, so I in my further education could persue the academic opportunities in Spanish language and culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned that when I started my courses, that 3/5 of my chosen and approoved courses was not even eligible for erasmus students. So during the biginning of the semester in september 2022 I had to completely changed my schedule so it fittet time wise. Also so it alined with the requirements of erasmus students. I wasn't able to finish reconstructing my entire erasmus course until the beginning of october in which i had already failed most of the mid-term exams.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find help at the university of Complutense, not so much the erasmus office back home in Copenhagen. They could only forward me to the erasmus office at the host university even though the mistake of informing som of the wrong courses to me came from the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office at the university Complutense in Madrid was very helpful. They informed me of the courses I could take that matched my own interests.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, I knew threw my parents a spanish couple who rented me their apartment througout my whole stay

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend looking online for housing like facebook groups etc. It is easier finding housing online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As soon as I arrived at the university we were informed to register at the Erasmus office. The proof of attendence paper was also given and signed at first arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The first day at my host university in Madrid there was an "intro day" for all the Erasmus students. We were then divided in groups so we would all get the different information that was relevant for our own course and registration, that was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Despite the University of Copenhagen providing wrong information about the courses that were available for Erasmus students from Denmark I was succesful in the final registration of courses I set in mid October 2022.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend triple checking the courses at the host university before even applying for an exchange. It is very important knowing what courses are offered at the host university and what is informed at your own university. Also i would recommend seeking out help about registration as soon as possible before start of the semester, because it might not be as you think.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was very interesting. But at the same time almost impossible to keep up with the level of academia at my host university in Madrid. There was no other Érasmus students in any of my classes, therefore there wasn't a lot of "care" of the fact that i didn't speak the language fluently yet and had not had a previous idea of what the spanish course of education is.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I explaned earlier in my additional comments of the academic programmed I found it very hard to keep up with the level of the courses since i did not know the language fully or the level of the Spanish academia. The professors and also the students did not seem to have the time or want to aid me in following the classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot more traditional than the teaching here in Copenhagen. Most of my proffesors helled their classes with a powerpoint and a lecture. Maybe there was time for a question or two at the end. But there was no discussions or group exersises during the classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Teoría de la Comunicación 
Historia del mundo actual
Historia del cine
Psicología de la comunicación
Arte contemporáneo

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend choosing something that alines with your interests, but also something that is manageable in the sense of level. And also choose a course where you know there will be other erasmus students, in that way you can "stick" with them and share your doubts and wants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of activities for Erasmus students travelling in Madrid including trips to different cities in Spain.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a long list of sport activities for all students, concerts and meet and greets for Erasmus students.
I went on a trip to Granada with some other Erasmus students for a weekend, it was amazing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Checking out the trips to other cities! It is usually planned trips by volunteers at the host university. But this also makes it a cheaper way of travel as you travel in a big group and also gets to meet new people, but also explore other parts of the country you're in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit cultural institutions of the city. Madrid for example is full of cultural gold and history for example el museo de Reina Sofia which is filled with art from the greatest like the "Guernica" Picasso and Salvador Dalí just to mention a few. Toledo, a town outside Madrid is also a beautiful small historic town filled with history.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: To look apart from my experience at the university it was fairly easy to adjust to the culture. I felt very much at home with the vibe. Also the culture in Madrid not that different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definately check out the events that are organized by the Erasmus volunteers, they make it very easy for you to meet other students, both local and Erasmus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the Spanish people, they don't really hover in my opinion compared to the danes. The Spanish have no problem voicing their opinions which i found very refreshing and honest.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check housing opportunities outside campus.

Go to events held by the Erasmus volonteers.

Triple check courses and their level before applying

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was definately the resistance I felt in the communication with UCPH. Their mail response was longer than expected, and not a lot of help came from it. I felt left alone in the sense that what i thought was done and approved from UCPH really wasn't. And when i let them know that all five of us that were on exchange at the same time had the same issues on arrival not a lot of help and guidance was given.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
